cut.description: First per-cut manifest for the tapes fixture corpus. An unversioned working-tree cut, not yet a tagged release.

provenance_bar: A fixture is admissible when it is synthetic-by-construction: either hand-authored, or a session recorded in a clean-room environment, credential-redacted, and reviewed. No customer content and no live production data.
notes: This manifest is the index for every tapes fixture family. It is deliberately the point of consolidation rather than a single physical directory: the derive corpora (~26 MB) are embedded (go:embed) by the demo seed, and a go:embed directive cannot reference a path above its own package. Homing them next to the seed keeps that 26 MB out of every binary that would import a shared top-level fixtures package. Each family records its physical `location`.
The four-layer pyramid (see README.md): L0 envelope -> L1 wire recordings -> L2 corpus -> L3 rendered API fixtures. Everything is generated downhill from one recording.

families.name: envelope
families.description: Header set -> expected parsed session envelope. Pins the X-Tapes-* header contract that any producer (a proxy injecting the headers) and any consumer (ingest, or another parser) must agree on.

provenance.notes: Hand-authored; no captured content. Header values are produced by a faithful port of the envelope encoding rules and self-checked against their pinned outputs.

consumers: tapes reader oracle: pkg/backfill/envelope_fixtures_test.go runs every case through sessionEnvelopeFromHeaders + Validate
paper (producer/encode side): crates/paper-daemon/src/proxy/headers_envelope_fixtures.rs, over a copy vendored at crates/paper-daemon/vendor/tapes-envelope-fixtures/
tapes-extproc (parser/decode side): internal/headers/envelope_fixtures_test.go, over a copy vendored at internal/headers/testdata/envelope/
any further producer/parser, via table tests over cases/*.json (vendor this directory to keep one copy authoritative)
families.consumer_note: The vendored copies are refreshed by each consumer's scripts/sync-envelope-fixtures.sh, which also detects drift (--check). A change to cases/*.json or README.md here is not live for those consumers until it is synced, and all copies should be refreshed from the same commit.

families.name: thread
families.description: Request header set -> resolved sub-thread id (meta.thread_id). Pins the harness-native thread-identity vocabulary — Claude's presence-list header and Codex's divergent thread-id/session-id pair with its root guard — whose canonical home is tapes-harnesses src/envelope.rs (HARNESS_THREAD_ID_RULES) with the lifecycle counterpart in src/attribution/codex_app.

provenance.notes: Hand-authored; synthetic repeated-digit UUIDs and obviously-fake agent ids only.

consumers: extproc reader + authored-home gate (oracle, DIGEST seal, rule coverage): extproc/headers/thread_corpus_test.go
tapes-harnesses (envelope::thread_id), via a vendored copy next to vendor/tapes-envelope-fixtures/ using the same sync + DIGEST mechanism
families.consumer_note: Same vendoring contract as the envelope family: one authoritative copy here, DIGEST-sealed; refresh every vendored copy from the same commit as the reader change it forces.

families.name: content-encoding
families.description: (body bytes, Content-Encoding value) -> decoded bytes, a reported salvage, or a classified error. Pins the captured-body decode POLICY rather than a header contract: which codings are readable, how stacked layers compose (peeled right-to-left), the 32 MiB per-layer output cap, the zstd window bound, and the two-conjunct salvage rule. The reference implementation is pkg/capture/contentencoding.go; the same policy is implemented independently in Rust in tapesctl (crates/tapesctl/src/start/content_encoding.rs).

provenance.notes: Hand-authored. Bodies are recipes (a plaintext plus the layers to apply) that each consumer compresses locally, because compressed output is not stable across implementations and pinning it would assert compressor identity rather than the policy. Byte-exact base64 is used only where the bytes are the assertion: two hand-built zstd frames differing solely in their window descriptor, two deliberately corrupt frames, and the empty body.

consumers: tapes reference oracle + authored-home gate (oracle, DIGEST seal, policy coverage): pkg/capture/contentencoding_corpus_test.go
tapesctl (Rust client decoder): crates/tapesctl/src/start/content_encoding.rs — NOT yet wired up; the corpus is the specification it should be wired to
families.consumer_note: Same vendoring contract as the envelope and thread families: one authoritative copy here, DIGEST-sealed; refresh every vendored copy from the same commit as the implementation change it forces.
families.why: PCC-1126: tapesctl dropped every content-encoding: zstd request body — all of Codex/pi's traffic — while the gateway route decoded the same bytes fine. Nothing was red, because the two implementations' agreement was a point-in-time claim by whoever last read both files.
contested_cases: limit-zstd-window-over-cap — Go bounds the zstd decoder with both max-window and max-memory; the Rust binding exposes window_log_max only. The corpus asserts the window bound (observable) and nothing about max-memory (not observable).

contested-empty-body-under-gzip — a bodiless request whose headers still claim an encoding. The decoder errors; not calling the decoder at all for a bodiless request is recorded as a CALLER PRECONDITION, which the tapesctl proxy's early return satisfies.

divergence-empty-body-under-zstd — the same empty body under zstd succeeds with zero bytes in the reference implementation. Recorded as observed and flagged as a suspected bug, not promoted to a rule.

families.name: recordings
families.description: Transport bytes for a turn, replayable across every ingest transport for parity checks. Each bundle is one request/response pair as the wire-trace recorder saw it: request headers plus base64 body, the verbatim (gzip) response stream, and the status/encoding/timing metadata.

provenance.generator: skills/generate-claude-fixture — a fixed-order, clean-room Claude Code session driven through a local clearing (kind-backed data plane, isolated paperd, PAPER_WIRE_TRACE_DIR).
provenance.clean_room: Launched from an empty /tmp directory that is not a git repository, with --strict-mcp-config (no MCP servers), --setting-sources project (no user-level skills or settings), and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1. Every file the session touched was created by the session itself under a scratch directory and deleted at the end. No repo reads, no git, no web, no MCP.
provenance.notes: All 17 bundles are POST /v1/messages. A single HEAD /api/hello health probe emitted by the harness in the same capture window was excluded: null content-type, zero-byte response, not a reducer input.

scrub_detail.headers: The recorder redacts CREDENTIAL headers to <redacted:<len>>. Verified across all bundles: authorization and x-paper-auth are redacted in every request; no unredacted credential header appears. x-api-key, anthropic-api-key and proxy-authorization are in the recorder's redact list but never appear on this capture path (the harness authenticates with an OAuth bearer in authorization), so they are untested here rather than confirmed. Note the scope: the recorder redacts credentials, NOT identifiers, and it does not touch response metadata at all — the provider-side identifiers in meta.json were left entirely to review, which is where they were initially missed. See substitution.
scrub_detail.bodies: Request bodies are NOT redacted by the recorder; the clean room is what keeps them clean. Reviewed in full: no home or workspace paths, no repository content, no git output (no gitStatus block is injected because the working directory is not a repository), no keys or tokens, no MCP tool definitions.
scrub_detail.substitution: Identifying values were replaced with synthetic stand-ins. In request BODIES the replacements are same-length, so content-length and body_peek_len stay valid and each bundle remains internally consistent: the operator address from the harness-injected `userEmail` system-reminder (22 bytes, once in each of 16 bundles); and the `device_id` (a stable 64-hex fingerprint of the capturing machine) and `account_uuid` inside the `metadata.user_id` blob Claude Code sends on every request. In response METADATA — meta.json's parsed response_headers, which are not wire bytes and carry no length constraint — `anthropic-organization-id`, `request-id`, `traceresponse` and `cf-ray` were replaced with synthetic values of the same shape. Response streams are untouched.
scrub_detail.substitution_rationale: None of these can be suppressed at capture time. CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL is only honored when no OAuth account is stored and an empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR fails to authenticate; device_id, account_uuid and the provider-side response headers are emitted unconditionally. They are identifiers rather than credentials — they authenticate nothing — but they identify the operator, their machine, and the tenant, and they let a reader correlate the corpus with provider telemetry, which is not acceptable in a corpus intended to be redistributable. Session ids are deliberately NOT substituted: they identify only this synthetic session and the envelope and sub-thread attribution the corpus exercises are keyed on them.
scrub_detail.enforcement: pkg/backfill/recordings_scrub_test.go is an executable gate over every committed bundle. It matches identifier FORMS — account/org UUIDs, device fingerprints, provider request ids, e-mail addresses, home paths, bearer/API credentials — rather than known values, so it fails on the next capture's leak rather than merely re-asserting that this one is clean. Synthetic stand-ins and the corpus's own session ids are allow-listed explicitly. The scrub bar is this test, not a reviewer's attention: the first pass of human review over these same bundles missed every identifier listed above.
scrub_detail.responses: Response streams were reviewed decompressed (they are gzip) and are clean on every pattern checked, including e-mail addresses, home paths and secrets.
scrub_detail.residual: noreply@anthropic.com and the string PCC-1003 remain in request bodies. Both are inert: the former is Claude Code's own commit-message boilerplate in the system prompt, the latter comes from the generator skill's own description. One /nix/store/<hash>-bash-5.3p9 path appears in a tool result — a public nixpkgs store path, not operator-identifying.

families.mcp_coverage: Deliberately absent. The session ran with no MCP servers configured, so no MCP tool definitions appear in any request and no MCP tool results are echoed into later turns. That is the trade this corpus makes: MCP tool-definition coverage is given up to keep bodies free of workspace data (real team, channel and issue names would otherwise be spread across many turns). Any test that needs MCP request shapes must use a separate, purpose-built fixture.

wire_shapes.sse_events: content_block_delta 580, content_block_start 41, content_block_stop 41, message_start 17, ping 17, message_delta 17, message_stop 17
wire_shapes.threading: 2 bundles carry x-claude-code-agent-id (a single Explore subagent), so the sub-thread attribution path is exercised.
wire_shapes.errors: Four tool-error results: command-not-found (exit 127), file-not-found (twice, once inside a parallel batch and once alone), invalid regex, and a failed Edit (string not found).
wire_shapes.absent: Sibling cancellation is NOT present. The generating skill's step 7 assumes the harness cancels the remaining tool calls in a batch when the first errors; in this harness and mode all three ran to completion and returned errors independently. Do not expect a cancellation shape from this set.

families.verification: Every bundle was replayed through capture.NewAnthropicReducer() via tapes-extproc's TestWireCaptureReducerFidelity: all 17 report EMPTY_CONTENT on the raw bytes and HEALTHY after the content-encoding decode (stop_reason tool_use x14, end_turn x3). That raw-empty/decoded-healthy contrast is a property of the set and is what the un-skipped test asserts.
consumers: tapes-extproc: TestWireCaptureReducerFidelity and TestWireCaptureProcessorFidelity (see that repo's testdata sync)
cross-transport parity checks over the ingest surfaces

families.name: derive-corpus
families.description: Gzipped raw_turns dumps of whole sessions. The deriver is a pure function of these rows, so the reconciliation pipeline regression-tests against them with no database.

provenance.notes: Full live Claude sessions captured through a gateway in a clean-room exercise: the wire envelopes as dispatched by the capture path plus each session's transcript files (main + subagents).
provenance.codex_notes: The two corpus-codex-* files are live captures through the July-22 codex_skills clearing gateway, re-shaped into the PCC-1021 post-fix attribution contract: every raw turn keyed to the ROOT Codex session id, the child thread id in meta.thread_id, and one transcript-source spawn-anchor row per child exactly as POST /v1/ingest/transcript mints it from the paperd uploader payload. corpus-codex-delta pins a root -> child (fork_turns:"all") -> grandchild chain; corpus-codex-parallel pins a seven-turn interleaved window of a 20-subagent session.

consumers: pkg/seed — demo seed (embeds the two-corpus seed_set only)
downstream client/UI test suites, via tapes dev trace-fixtures
families.embed_note: Physically homed under pkg/seed so the demo seed can go:embed the seed_set (embed can't cross '..'), keeping the 26 MB out of non-seed binaries. corpus-0440f43d is co-located and used by the derive gates and the fixture generator, but deliberately NOT in the seed_set: it is a much larger, many-session capture, and seeding it would triple the embedded payload and change the demo session count. The corpus-codex-* pair is likewise co-located and NOT in the seed_set: they exist to pin the Codex subagent-nesting projection, not to seed demos.

families.name: capture-reducer
families.description: Provider wire (streaming SSE and one-shot JSON) that drives the reducer tests, including oneshot<->stream pairs that must reduce to the same content hash.

provenance.anthropic: hand-crafted against the Anthropic Messages streaming spec (not recorded traffic); stable placeholder ids (msg_FIXTURE..., toolu_FIXTURE...).
provenance.openai_responses: real Responses wire recorded through a gateway, including the Codex chatgpt stream.

consumers: any external service that embeds the same reducers

families.name: rendered-api
families.location: consuming client/UI repositories (generated, not stored here)
families.description: The session -> traces -> spans projection rendered exactly as the API serves it, for client/UI test suites that want to stay language-independent of the deriver.

provenance.notes: tapes dev trace-fixtures replays the derive corpora through the real deriver and the real API renderers with deterministic session ids.

families.scrub_attestation: derived from the derive-corpus family; no independent capture
families.freshness: Matches projection_schema_version 2026-06-15; regenerate when the deriver or renderers change.
